Subject: POC scope & evaluation method selection — next steps and owners

Thanks again for the time today, Priya and Anil — good chat. Quick recap and a proposal for the POC / evaluation approach so we can lock the kickoff and owners. Please correct anything I missed.

High-level goal:
- Validate Redwood inference for clinical triage augmentation in Medisys intake flow (reduce triage latency; surface high-confidence suggestions to clinicians).

Proposed POC structure (2 parts):
1) 2-week online shadow run (live traffic, no clinician-facing changes) — primary readouts: latency, throughput, real-time confidence distribution, and top-1 suggestion agreement with existing triage logic.
2) 1-week offline evaluation on a curated stratum of historical cases (edge cases, PHI-scrubbed examples) — primary readouts: precision/recall for high-confidence labels, failure mode examples for review.

Suggested success criteria (draft — we'll iterate):
- Top-1 agreement with existing triage: >= 85% across non-urgent cases
- High-confidence suggestion precision (confidence >= 0.8): >= 90% on sampled human-reviewed cases
- 95th percentile end-to-end latency (in-shadow): <= 300ms
- No PHI exfiltration; PII/PHI handling validated in Private deployment checklist

Evaluation method choice rationale:
- Shadow first lets us validate latency and distribution under real load without rolling changes to clinicians.
- Offline eval lets us run controlled scoring and heavier human review on edge cases where labeling is ambiguous.

Owners / immediate asks:
- Medisys: confirm the 2-week shadow window and identify a smaller gateway for the shadow traffic (Anil).
- Redwood infra: set up shadow routing and metrics collection (Karthik).
- Redwood CS/ops: coordinate data access, PHI handling, and kickoff logistics (Marissa, Vanessa).

Next steps / proposed timeline:
- This week: Medisys confirms scope and sample size (target: 5k shadow requests/day or equivalent window).
- Week of May 17: infra prep and security checklist; dry run.
- Week of May 24: begin 2-week shadow.

Attachments: I attached a draft success criteria spreadsheet and our trial playbook.

Thanks — I can walk through the success criteria on a quick call if helpful.

—Sean

Thanks Sean — high level alignment looks good. Couple of clarifications from our side:

1) PHI & deployment mode: we cannot send any live PHI to a hosted environment. We will only accept Shadow if Redwood runs it in our VPC/private deployment or if we provide a PHI-scrubbed proxy. Can Karthik confirm options?

2) Timeline: the dates look feasible but we need to align with our security review. Can we push the shadow start to May 31 if necessary?

3) Success criteria: the 85% top-1 agreement looks reasonable for baseline, but we also need a fall-back SLA if false positives exceed 5% in human-reviewed samples.

4) Sample size: we'll start with a 48-hour burst of mirrored traffic (pilot) to validate routing and telemetry, then scale to the 2-week window.

I'll loop in our compliance lead if we move forward; otherwise this looks like a good plan.

Thanks, all — short technical notes and a suggested grading rubric so the team can agree before kickoff.

1) Deployment & PHI handling:
- We support Private (VPC) shadow routing and an on-prem connector for PHI-sensitive traffic. Option A: Shadow traffic remains in Medisys VPC and we stream telemetry to Redwood monitoring (no raw PHI leaves). Option B: Redwood processes within customer-managed enclave; logs are hashed/filtered.

2) Metrics & instrumentation (what we'll collect during shadow):
- request_id, routing_zone, model_variant, request_latency_ms (end-to-end), token_count, top-5 predictions + confidences, decision_flag (match/mismatch with baseline), sample_payload_hash (for traceability).
- We'll also export a periodic sample of de-identified payloads for human review.

3) Grading rubric (proposed — please comment):
- Primary: Top-1 agreement (weighted by urgency bucket) — pass if >= 85%
- Safety: High-confidence precision (confidence >= 0.8) — pass if >= 90%
- Latency: 95th percentile E2E <= 300ms — pass if met for >= 95% of requests in non-burst windows
- False positive ceiling: human-reviewed FP rate <= 5% in sampled population — must be below threshold or trigger rollback
- Uncertain cases: if model confidence in [0.4,0.8], route to human-in-loop for display only and track disagreement rate

4) Offline eval plan (what we'll do during the 1-week static run):
- Curate 2k historical cases with balanced urgency and edge-case representation
- Use automated scoring to compute precision/recall, then 200-case human adjudication sample for error analysis

5) Ownership matrix (short):
- Infra & routing: Karthik (Redwood)
- Security & compliance coordination: Marissa (Redwood) + Medisys compliance lead (TBD)
- Data sampling & human review coordination: Vanessa (Redwood) + Priya (Medisys)
- Evaluation analysis & final report: Redwood Solutions (Karthik + Marissa)

I'll prepare a small script that calculates top-1/top-5 agreement and sample exports for human review — will share in Drive by EOD.

—Karthik
Principal Engineer, Inference Platform
